1.why: All six screens show a static, uncluttered layout with no animations, carousels, or pop-ups.

2.why: Teal primary buttons, bold headings, and highlighted info boxes make the main actions and fields stand out clearly.

3.why: Each step has a single obvious purpose, labeled fields, and one primary button, so the next action is immediately findable.

4.why: The user must recall password complexity rules (12+ chars, upper, lower, number, symbol) and transcribe multiple one-time codes across steps.

5.why: No password-manager hints, autofill affordances, or “remember me” controls appear on any screen.

6.why: Aside from the demo-account tip, the screens show no saved credentials, familiar devices, or previously used items to recognize.

7.why: Labels and instructional sentences are brief, plain-language, and easy to scan on every step.

8.why: No error states or error messages are shown in any of the six screenshots, so the claim cannot be verified as true.

9.why: Explicit examples are given: “use demo-account”, password composition rules, and the actual test/MFA codes displayed in the logs panel.

10.why: The flow never presents alternative authentication choices such as password versus code versus face login; only the fixed reset path is shown.

11.why: Each screen offers at most one primary action and one secondary action (e.g., “Request another code”), avoiding choice overload.

12.why: Info banners, updating logs, and the final “Password recovery complete” page explicitly state the result of each step.

13.why: Short tips appear on every step (code expiry, privacy note, password rules, security warnings, log-panel instructions).

14.why: “Request another code” and “Return to recovery start” buttons allow re-attempts, though no inline validation-retry UI is visible.

15.why: Header, card layout, color scheme, typography, and logs panel remain identical across all six steps.
